_doc: Candid per-pose verdicts, written after looking at the review sheet of each pose (tools/bt/photomatch/reports/<pose>.jpg). Allowed: matches, roughly, does not, cannot judge. matches = the render at the registered pose reproduces horizon height, the order and spacing of the named landmarks and the visible structures to within about a tenth of the frame without any parameter set from the photograph; roughly = the large-scale layout agrees but the offsets are larger than that; does not = the layout contradicts the photograph; cannot judge = nothing comparable is in the frame or the pose leaves nothing to test. A verdict of matches or roughly needs reviewed_image = true. independent_test = false where a number (the distance) was read from the photograph: such a pose is never called a match and carries no weight for the gate. Every verdict is conditional on the registered pose, none is a finding about the 1863 landscape alone. Photograph-level verdicts for all 191 records are in photograph_registry.json. Third pass (2026-11-14): for the poses at a documented camera place (P27, P28, P29) the pass criteria were written before the render and are in criteria.json; a verdict may be stricter than the letter of a criterion (the binary tests are necessary conditions) and never looser; a test that fits parameters to the photograph (the skyline test fits the heading inside the NPS sector, the lens and a vertical shift) can support a pose but never makes a verdict matches. Poses superseded by a better-sourced pose keep their verdicts (P06 by P28, P07 by P27); the photograph-level verdict of a record is the verdict of its current pose.
reviewed: 2026-11-13: review sheets P01, P03, P06 to P09, P11, P12, P13, P17 to P20, P24, P26 viewed; P04 and P05 as in the first run (2026-11-11). 2026-11-14: P13 verdict written, sheets and lines images of P27 and P28 viewed. 2026-11-15: sheet and lines image of P29 viewed and its verdict written; all 20 pose sheets (P01 to P29) and the lines images of P27, P28 and P29 opened and looked at again, and every verdict read against its sheet (the renders were reproduced byte for byte). 2026-11-16: all 20 pose sheets (P01 to P29), the lines images of P27, P28 and P29 and the 50 degree lines images of P27 and P28 were opened and looked at again in the fifth session and every verdict was read against its sheet; none changed (the 120 renders were reproduced byte for byte a second time; the sheets rebuilt by compose.py are byte-identical to the earlier ones).

pose_verdicts.why: Far field at the registered pose (Warren statue summit, heading 7.8 deg, 40 deg field): the model horizon sits at 0.51 of the frame height, the photograph's far ridge and groves at about 0.44 (read by eye, +-0.02), about 3 degrees higher. The landmarks the NPS names fall in the NPS order (Codori house, High Water Mark monument for the Copse, Ziegler's Grove, Cemetery Hill) but 40 to 110 px of a 480-px panel (3 to 9 degrees) left of the features they should mark, the error growing to the right, so the spacing is about 1.8 times too narrow at 40 degrees (the 30 degree render is closer: a longer lens is likely, undocumented). The boulder, pine and stump of the near field are not in the model. Pose, lens and terrain errors cannot be separated. The Patterson stand-in lies 31 degrees right of Cemetery Hill, outside any frame, so it cannot be tested (EG-11).

The 2023 gatehouse outline (25.8 m wide, default one storey, lodge and pavilion merged) is placed in front of the facade with its distance read from the photograph (fitted), so its width and place agree by construction (boxes at 0.27 to 0.82 of the frame width against the arch building's 0.10 to 0.76, tops at 3.2 m against a two-storey building with towers); the only independent items, the horizon height (0.48 against about 0.46) and a face-on facade, follow from the same footprint. Nothing is left to test.

Standpoint on Seminary Ridge looking at the borough is contradicted by the photograph itself: a large cupola building and the town appear at distance with a road curving across the foreground, i.e. the camera stands further out; only 'from the West' is in the caption, no position. The render has the borough masses on the horizon only. Horizon 0.50 vs photo 0.38. (Carried over from the first run, 2026-11-11: the pose and the render are unchanged. Third pass, 2026-11-14: this photograph is the left plate of the two-plate panorama that the Library of Congress print 2014646002 (View of Gettysburg from the Northwest) joins: image match with 209 inliers, same-plate geometry, the footprint covers 0.00 to 0.53 of the print's width; both images were looked at. The Library caption says only 'from the Northwest', so the Seminary Ridge standpoint of this pose is still an assumption and the verdict is on that assumed pose, not on a camera position that is known.)

Same assumed pose as P04 although the two photographs have different standpoints (P05 has a brick house in the near middle ground). One pose cannot be right for both; the caption gives no position. Horizon 0.50 vs photo 0.38. (Carried over from the first run, 2026-11-11: the pose and the render are unchanged. Third pass, 2026-11-14: this photograph is the right plate of the two-plate panorama that the Library of Congress print 2014646002 (View of Gettysburg from the Northwest) joins: image match with 213 inliers, same-plate geometry, the footprint covers 0.45 to 0.96 of the print's width; both images were looked at. The Library caption says only 'from the Northwest', so the Seminary Ridge standpoint of this pose is still an assumption and the verdict is on that assumed pose, not on a camera position that is known.)

At the registered pose (East Cemetery Hill, Wiedrich monument plus 25 m east, looking to the borough) the model puts every building in a narrow band at the horizon (0.52 of the frame height) and shows no road; the photograph has the Baltimore Pike running from the lower left to the town at left centre, houses spread over the full frame width, a ridge behind them at 0.47 and a tent camp at the right. The apparent size and spread of the town differ by about a factor of 2: the camera was nearer the town and lower on the slope than assumed (sigma 150 m), and the model holds only 2023 outlines of surviving buildings. The verdict is on this pose only.

The same assumed cemetery pose as P06 and the same result: the frame is a stereo sibling of P06 (road at the left, tents at the right, the town across the horizon) and the render shows a narrow band of footprints at the horizon and no road. Pose-conditional, as P06.

The title names the place (about the right gun of Wiedrich's Battery, at the monument) but no direction. At the placeholder heading of 45 degrees the render shows open ground and the east edge of the town; the photograph shows a steepled house at the right and a pine at the centre across a wall-lined field. Another heading would be a free parameter set by the photograph itself, so the pose cannot be tested.

Silhouette of Big Round Top from the assumed spot on the south slope of Little Round Top (statue point, 35 m south, heading 202 deg toward the gazetteer centre of Big Round Top): the photograph's hill has its summit at 0.38 of the frame width and 0.28 of its height with a broad right flank; the model's cone has its summit at 0.42 and 0.43, i.e. about 15 percent of the frame height (5 degrees) lower, and a narrower top. The horizontal place and the kind of silhouette agree; the vertical offset fits a camera lower on the slope than assumed (the spot is only known as the southern slope, sigma 60 m) and the forest canopy that the bare DEM lacks. Pose and terrain errors cannot be separated.

Same assumed spot and heading as P09, a different exposure: the photograph's Big Round Top has its summit at 0.44 of the frame width and 0.29 of its height with a broad, gentle left shoulder; the model's has it at 0.42 and 0.44 and a steeper, narrower cone. Same reading as P09: place and kind of silhouette agree, the model's summit is about 15 percent of the frame height lower, a camera spot lower on the slope and the tree canopy would account for it.

The title says Big Round Top is in the background, but in the photograph the hill is not visible: trees and haze fill the upper third behind a breastwork and boulder that take the foreground. The render shows a clear cone in that direction that the frame does not let one check.

Valley of Death view at the registered pose (250 m west of the gazetteer centre of the Wheatfield Road crossing, an assumption with sigma 200 m; heading 150 degrees chosen from the title's content so that both named hills fall inside a 40-degree field, 1.6 m above the ground): the order and kind of silhouette agree (Little Round Top as a broad swell at the left and centre, Big Round Top at the right edge) but the photograph's crest line stands at 0.25 to 0.30 of the frame height and the model's at about 0.40 (the horizon row of the render is 0.412): about 0.12 to 0.14 of the frame, 4 degrees, higher in the photograph; the summit of Big Round Top is at 0.88 of the frame width in the photograph and 0.99 in the render. The boulder-strewn west slope, the pines and the foreground are not in the model. The offsets are of the size that a camera about 200 m nearer to Little Round Top (the sigma of the assumed spot) would give, so pose and terrain errors cannot be separated; the crossing of Wheatfield Road and Crawford Avenue that the NPS names is not in the model.

The Thompson house footprint (2023 outline, default one storey) is placed south-south-west of the house with its distance read from the photograph (fitted), so its width and place agree by construction (0.26 to 0.81 against 0.19 to 0.83 of the frame). The model shows the long south facade face-on and 3.2 m high; the photograph shows a three-quarter view with the gable at the right and a 1.5-storey roof. The NPS fixes the direction (looking north across the turnpike) but not the bearing, so the difference of about 30 degrees is the assumed bearing, not a fault of the model. Nothing independent is left.

Leister house at the end of the Taneytown Road: the footprint sits where the house is (centred by construction, distance fitted), and two items that were not fitted agree: the road line runs from the house to the lower right as in the photograph, and the horizon is at 0.46 against 0.52. The orchard, the stone wall, the fences and the trees are not in the model; the test is not independent for the footprint.

The Bryan house footprint (6.0 by 7.6 m, 1.5 storeys, 2023 outline) is placed east-south-east of the house with the distance read from the photograph (fitted): the wire box fills the frame about as the house does, but has no roof, lean-to or bake-oven shed; nothing independent can be compared. Whether this record is the NPS Brien Farm report's photograph taken east of the house looking west is not established (caption only).

The Schmucker Hall footprint (47.9 by 44.3 m, the 2023 outline) is placed 190 m west with the distance read from the photograph (fitted); it shows as a thin strip at the horizon about 0.12 of the frame width left of the building in the photograph, which is inside what the camera spot (sigma 50 m at 190 m is 15 degrees) allows. The model has no cupola, storeys or fence. Nothing independent can be compared.

Trostle farm: the house footprint is placed south-west of the pair with its distance read from the photograph (fitted); the barn footprint, which was not used in the fit, falls at the far left edge of the frame, where a small gabled outbuilding (the barn, far behind the yard) stands in the photograph: the barn-to-house baseline and the angular spread agree. One item contradicts: the framework left of the house (the NPS: an 1863 addition) is left of the house in the photograph, while the model's summer-kitchen footprint lies about 13 m to the right of the house from this side (EG-12). Roof, trees, fences and the dead horses are not in the model.

Same as P03 for the other gatehouse view (Brady, about two weeks after the battle): the 2023 outline is placed in front of the facade with its distance read from the photograph (fitted), boxes at 0.32 to 0.75 of the frame width against the building's 0.30 to 0.9, tops at 3.2 m; the horizon height and a face-on facade follow from the same footprint. The pavilion beside the gatehouse (a separate point in the model) is not drawn. Nothing independent is left to test.

numbers.rule_outcome_of_C1: matches (T1, T2 and T3 pass at the registered heading and the 40 degree field)

pose_verdicts.why: First test at a documented camera place. Place: the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge (NPS Cemetery CLR Fig. 1.26, LC-B815-273 = this record), the centroid of the 2023 outline of the gatehouse, sigma 20 m, 8 m above the ground (assumed); heading north = 0 degrees (the NPS word); field 40 degrees (assumed). The record is a stereo negative; the Sketch Book print of the same view (record 2014646001, pose P28) matches its frames with one homography at about 1 px residual at every depth, so the station is the same. At the registered heading 0 degrees and the 40 degree field: T1 (pike in the left 55 percent of the frame) True (pike at 0.026 to 0.261 of the frame width, 52 visible vertices); T2 (horizon within 0.10 of 0.47) True (render 0.534); T3 (town band centre in 0.05 to 0.60) True (building outlines centre 0.462, GZ-072 at 0.218). By the letter of the criterion written before the render that is a match. The same criterion calls the three tests necessary conditions, and the same measurement passes all three for the superseded poses P06 and P07, whose verdict is does not, so they cannot carry a match alone. Looking at the sheet and at the model lines laid on the photograph (reports/P27_lines.jpg): the centre line of the Baltimore Pike lies inside the road of the photograph from the lower left to the left edge, the model's building outlines stand at the left of the horizon where the town is, and the render has no tents, walls, fences or trees. Skyline test (C-P27-P28-2, heading free inside the sector, lens and vertical shift free): RMS 0.0938 degrees at heading -0.5 and field 25 (match-level); the station ranks 14 of 25 against 24 control stations 100 to 300 m away (controls 0.0895 to 0.2873, first quartile 0.0934), discriminated = False; camera height 5 m and 11 m: RMS 0.0936 and 0.0939. Exploratory, not a test: the courthouse clock tower (identified by looking: the model note says about 70 ft clock tower) stands at 0.737 of the width of the Sketch Book print, and the model's courthouse outline would stand at 0.25 of the frame at the registered heading; the tower implies a heading of 337.2 to 342.5 degrees (field 50 to 30 degrees), at the boundary of the NPS words north and northwest. Verdict: roughly, conditional on the pose: the road side, the town band and the horizon agree, the landmark that can be read does not fall within a tenth of the frame at the registered heading, the model cannot supply individual structures to compare, and nothing here is a registration against T-Q16-1 (unset). Fifth pass (2026-11-16): Gardner's own letterpress for plate 35 of the Sketch Book (the Library's digitized album, page 77, read from the master scan with text recognition and by eye; statement PS-GARDNER-SB1-P77) says: 'This view is taken from Cemetery Ridge, where our artillery was massed' and that Seminary Ridge 'can be seen' 'on the left of the picture'. It is a second source for the place, in the photographer's own words; it is consistent with the National Park Service place (the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge on the cemetery knoll at the Baltimore Pike; Gardner's text for plate 39 calls the knoll of the National Soldiers' Cemetery Cemetery Ridge, but he also uses the name for the ridge toward Round Top) and it does not fix the building; it gives no spot, no bearing, no height and no lens, so the position stays inferred and no count changes. As a cue for the direction it is not a test (found after the renders were looked at) and changes nothing: at the north heading of this pose and the assumed 40 degree field the left edge of the frame is 340 degrees, so the gazetteer centre of Seminary Ridge (302.4 degrees from the gatehouse) and the Seminary building (313.8) lie outside it (x -0.94 and -0.65 of the frame width); at the northwest heading of pose P28 they lie at 0.18 and 0.47. The verdict (roughly) rests on the criterion written before the render and is unchanged.

numbers.rule_outcome_of_C1: not defined by the rule (T1 fails, T2 passes, T3 disagrees); the conservative reading is used: not matches, not roughly

pose_verdicts.why: Same place and exposure as P27 (the Sketch Book print plate 35; a second print of it is record 2006685383); heading northwest = 315 degrees (the NPS word of the Record of Treatment, volumes I and II: a view northwest from Cemetery Hill); field 40 degrees (assumed). At the registered heading 315 degrees and the 40 degree field: T1 (pike in the left 55 percent of the frame) False (pike at 0.872 to 0.994 of the frame width, 40 visible vertices); T2 (horizon within 0.10 of 0.47) True (render 0.514); T3 (town band centre in 0.05 to 0.60) disagree (building outlines centre 0.579, GZ-072 at outside the frame, right). The criterion written before the render defines matches (all three pass), roughly (T2 and one of T1, T3 pass) and does not (T1 and T2 fail together, or the pike on the wrong side at both words); this combination (T1 fails, T2 passes, T3 disagrees) is not covered, so the conservative reading is taken: not matches, not roughly. By the sheet and the lines laid on the photograph (reports/P28_lines.jpg) the layout contradicts the photograph: at 315 degrees the Baltimore Pike lies at the right edge of the frame (0.87 to 0.99 of the width; out of the frame at the 30 degree field) and the town outlines stand in the right half, while in the photograph the pike runs from the lower left to the left of the centre and the town lies at the left and centre. Skyline test (C-P27-P28-2, heading free inside the sector, lens and vertical shift free): RMS 0.1043 degrees at heading -24.5 and field 25 (match-level); the station ranks 14 of 25 against 24 control stations 100 to 300 m away (controls 0.0795 to 0.2917, first quartile 0.1041), discriminated = False; camera height 5 m and 11 m: RMS 0.1042 and 0.1045. Verdict: does not, conditional on the heading word northwest (315 degrees) read at the centre of its sector; read from the photograph the heading lies at the boundary of the two NPS words (the exploratory courthouse reading in numbers), so the centre of northwest is about 20 degrees off. Fifth pass (2026-11-16): Gardner's own letterpress for plate 35 of the Sketch Book (the Library's digitized album, page 77, read from the master scan with text recognition and by eye; statement PS-GARDNER-SB1-P77) says: 'This view is taken from Cemetery Ridge, where our artillery was massed' and that Seminary Ridge 'can be seen' 'on the left of the picture'. It is a second source for the place, in the photographer's own words; it is consistent with the National Park Service place (the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge on the cemetery knoll at the Baltimore Pike; Gardner's text for plate 39 calls the knoll of the National Soldiers' Cemetery Cemetery Ridge, but he also uses the name for the ridge toward Round Top) and it does not fix the building; it gives no spot, no bearing, no height and no lens, so the position stays inferred and no count changes. As a cue for the direction it is not a test (found after the renders were looked at) and changes nothing: at this pose's northwest heading and 40 degree field the gazetteer centre of Seminary Ridge (302.4 degrees from the gatehouse) stands at 0.18 of the frame width and the Seminary building (313.8) at 0.47, so the left-of-picture phrase is met at the northwest word and not at the north word of pose P27; but the same heading fails the pike test and puts the court house (349.6 degrees) outside the frame at x 1.37, while the photograph shows a tower at 0.737 of its width. The two National Park Service words and Gardner's phrase are carried as three readings that no single heading meets at 40 degrees; the free heading read from the tower (337.2 to 342.5 degrees, exploratory_heading.json, a fit and not a test) puts Oak Ridge (339.8) at x 0.5, the Seminary building at x -0.15 (outside the left edge) and the court house at x 0.74. None is chosen. The verdict (does not) rests on the criterion written before the render and is unchanged.

Second documented camera place: the gatehouse (NPS Record of Treatment vol. I, Figure 213: View east from Evergreen Cemetery Gatehouse, 1863, park print GETT 41135 OS2B-2037, which is this record by image match: 661 inliers, both images looked at), the centroid of the 2023 outline of the building, sigma 20 m, 8 m above the ground (assumed); heading east = 90 degrees (the NPS word, sector 67.5 to 112.5); field 40 degrees (assumed). The record's own caption says the lunettes in the foreground covered the guns of Reynolds' battery and the entrenchments on the side of the hill were Wadsworth's line (Culp's Hill). The criterion written before the render (C-P29-1) is the skyline test only, because the NPS word east fixes the heading to 45 degrees and the near field is not in the model. Result: RMS 0.5608 degrees (partial: above the 0.5 degrees of match-level) at heading 93.25 (inside the sector) and field 25 (the lower end of the range) with a vertical shift of -140.1 px (the figure is a crop of unknown vertical extent); the station ranks 19 of 25 against 24 control stations 100 to 300 m away (RMS 0.2082 to 0.8051, first quartile 0.4379, median 0.5393), so 18 of the 24 control stations fit better than the gatehouse and 6 fit worse (the rank counts from the best fit): discriminated = False. The best-fitting stations lie at 300 m bearing 135 (ground 167.52 m, RMS 0.2082), 200 m bearing 90 (ground 169.51 m, RMS 0.2403), 300 m bearing 90 (ground 167.0 m, RMS 0.2866), lower than the gatehouse ground (186.14 m) by 16.6 to 19.1 m; at 1007 m (the distance to the gazetteer centre of Culp's Hill) such a height is about 0.9 to 1.1 degrees, the size of the residual. A camera lower than assumed or a hill taller than the bare-earth model's (tree cover would do it, but no source read gives the 1863 canopy height of Culp's Hill) has the same effect, so the test cannot say which. By the rule written before the render (S1 partial or S2 false) the skyline neither supports nor contradicts the place. Sheet and lines image looked at (reports/P29.jpg, reports/P29_lines.jpg). At the registered pose (heading 90 degrees, field 40 degrees, level camera, 8 m) the render is a smooth bare-earth swell without trees, earthworks, fence or tent; its highest point stands at 0.7 of the frame width and 0.486 of its height. The figure shows a wooded hill whose crest stands at 0.711 of the width and 0.179 of the height (frozen skyline rule), with lower ground at the left (skyline at 0.303 of the height at the left edge) and, in the foreground, the lunettes, a field with plants, a fence and a tent, which the model does not have. Read at the registered pose the order agrees (a hill to the right of the centre, falling to the left; the crest is 0.011 of the frame width apart, which at one registered field and one hill is partly luck, the 30 and 50 degree renders put it at 0.777 and 0.653); the height does not: the render's crest is 0.307 of the frame height lower than the photograph's, and the crest rises 0.047 of the height above the left edge in the render against 0.124 in the photograph. The figure is a crop of unknown vertical extent of a camera whose tilt is unknown (the photograph looks down on the foreground), so that offset cannot be assigned to the pose, the lens or the terrain. The one road line of the model inside the frame (cyan, at the left) lies on the wood line, where the photograph shows no road. The agreement is therefore weak: one hill silhouette, no structure, and no test that tells this station from its neighbours. Verdict: roughly, conditional on the pose and weak: at the registered pose the order of the silhouette agrees (a wooded hill right of the centre, lower ground at the left) and its height does not; after the three parameters fitted from the photograph the silhouettes agree to 0.5608 degrees RMS with the heading inside the NPS sector; nothing here shows that the gatehouse is a better station than its neighbours (the test does not discriminate), and a fit with three free parameters cannot make a match.

reason: The gate asks for tests at known camera positions. Under the standing decision DD-PM-01 a documented camera position is a coordinate, a lens and a plate that a source other than a lead gives: none of the catalogued photographs has one; the 161 camera-position statements read (Library of Congress records, National Park Service reports, place pages and the Record of Treatment, and the photographer's own printed words of 1863 and 1866) give words (place, direction, reference object), never a coordinate, a lens or a surveyed station (the Library's physical description gives the plate type of the stereo negatives, and a plate size of 4 x 10 in. for 16 of them, among them the lodge-roof exposure; no record gives a lens).

The first documented camera places exist: the National Park Service names the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge for the view of Gettysburg to the north (records 2018671576 and 2014646001: poses P27 north and P28 northwest, two words of two NPS texts for one exposure) and the gatehouse for the view east (record 2012647704: pose P29). Their height, lens and exact heading are not documented (height assumed 8 m, lens assumed 40 degrees, the heading a cardinal word with a 45-degree sector), so their position tier stays inferred and they are counted apart (3 poses).

The pass criteria of the tests at those places were written before the renders (criteria.json). Results: P27 roughly, P28 does not, P29 roughly. The three binary tests of the first criterion are necessary conditions only (they are also passed by the superseded poses P06 and P07, whose verdict is does not), and the skyline test fits the heading, the lens and a vertical shift to the photograph, so no pose is called a match and none can be: a fitted test is not a match, and the registration against T-Q16-1 is not possible while T-Q16-1 is unset.

The model has no 1863 near field (trees, rocks, crops, fences, woods edges): only far silhouettes, mapped building footprints at a default height and roads can be compared. Where the model and a photograph disagree (3 to 9 degrees in the cases examined) the disagreement cannot be assigned to the pose, the lens or the terrain.
The NPS plate that labels the landmarks of the view from Little Round Top could not be mapped to the photograph, and the landmark stand-ins in the repository carry 221 to 300 m of uncertainty.

Fifth pass (2026-11-16): the Library's records were read again from the open JSON (191 of 191 fetched, none changed since the first reading) and every sentence that names a place or direction of view was listed (loc_reread_20261116.json); the letterpress of Gardner's Sketch Book for the ten Gettysburg plates (35 to 44) was read from the master scans with text recognition: one plate (35, the exposure of poses P27 and P28) says where the view was taken (Cemetery Ridge, Seminary Ridge on the left), none gives a coordinate, a lens or a plate. Gardner's catalogue of September 1863 (Library copy) and the Library's essays 'Does the Camera Ever Lie?' were read: titles, numbers and credits, and leads attributed to Frassanito. The count of documented camera positions stays 0 and the gate does not pass.
what_is_needed: Camera station coordinates from the body that has them: the Gettysburg National Military Park took its Then-And-Now pictures from the same locations as the originals (the park says so) and its Historic Photograph Collection (GETT 41135) holds the prints that the Record of Treatment cites by number (2B-2063, 2B-2090, 2B2001, OS2B-2037 and about thirty more): its museum or GIS staff may hold the station, the lens and the plate of each; or Frassanito's published positions (copyrighted: needs the owner's decision to buy, borrow or ask permission). Either gives a documented position with a stated accuracy.

For the exposures made from the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse (P27, P28, P29): the height and the spot on the building (the roof, a window), the 1863 form of the building (the model holds the 2023 outline with its right-hand addition; the NPS cemetery report says that the lodge of 1855 is a two-story archway with two floors of lodge quarters in the flanking piers and that a two-story frame addition on the rear was built after the battle, but it gives no height in metres and does not say which part of the outline is the addition), and the lens and plate of the exposures; a drawing or photograph of the lodge of 1855 from the Evergreen Cemetery Association or the park archive.

The lens (focal length) of each exposure; the plate is documented only in part (the Library gives glass stereograph plates and, for 16 negatives, a size of 4 x 10 in.; the large-format views and most stereo negatives have no size), or a calibration from straight edges and from two or more mapped landmarks of known coordinates in the same photograph; for the skyline of Gettysburg from the cemetery, a source that names the towers and cupolas in the photograph (the courthouse clock tower, the college and church cupolas) so that they can be used as landmarks.

A model of the 1863 near field where a photograph is to be matched: trees, rocks (Devil's Den, Little Round Top, the Rose Woods), walls and fences, crop state, tents: the R12 vegetation and rock layers.

Landmark coordinates good to a few metres for the objects the captions and the NPS name (Ziegler's Grove, the Copse, the Brien lane tree, Codori Grove, the Patterson house, the McPherson quarry, Seminary Lane, the Foulk farm, the crossing of Wheatfield Road and Crawford Avenue, the Baltimore Street entrance of the national cemetery); the gazetteer centres carry 221 to 300 m.

A decision on whether a building named by a non-lead source with a cardinal word counts as a documented camera position (DD-PM-06 says it does not: the gate keeps its wording) and a value for T-Q16-1 (unset), written before the match; a reviewer who did not set the pose and who looks at every sheet; the criterion and the failures recorded per photograph (PDF B.9.2 step 7).

Full-resolution masters of the photographs to be matched (25 to 130 MB each; 2 of about 490 resources fetched, kept as 4096-px working copies) and a clean scan of the NPS annotated enlargement of the view north from Little Round Top.
owner_steps: Ask the Gettysburg National Military Park museum or GIS office (a third party: an owner act) for the station coordinates and the camera and lens of its Then-And-Now pictures and for the catalogue entries of the Historic Photograph Collection prints that the Record of Treatment cites (list in tools/bt/photomatch/nps_figures.json; among them the prints taken from the Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse, the Rose Barn, McPherson Farm and Little Round Top; GNMP SF-2B-2087, SF-2B-2090, SF-2B-2095, SF-28-2083, 2B2001).
Ask the Evergreen Cemetery Association (a third party: an owner act) for the form and height of the gatehouse in 1863 and the park archive for the lodge drawings of 1855.

Decide whether to buy or borrow Frassanito's Early Photography at Gettysburg (billing is an owner act) or to ask the publisher in writing for the right to use its camera positions; until then no camera position that rests on it is used.

Decide the default reading of the lodge-roof view (north in the Cemetery report, northwest in the Record of Treatment; both are carried as P27 and P28, none is chosen here), whether a named building roof counts as a documented camera position (DD-PM-06) and the value of T-Q16-1.
A NARA catalog API key (an account: an owner act) would let the Brady and Gardner descriptions of the National Archives be read; not requested here.
